key_insight: Training one model on diverse modalities yields "Context Unrolling": the model explicitly performs an intermediate, iterative cross-modal reasoning step that aggregates heterogeneous representations before making predictions, improving fidelity to shared multimodal knowledge.
problem_solved: Multimodal systems often fail to faithfully combine complementary signals across text, image, video, 3D and latent representations; this work addresses the lack of an explicit internal aggregation process for joint multimodal reasoning.
method: Native unified training of a single Omni model across heterogeneous modalities (text, images, videos, 3D geometry, hidden/latent reps).
Introduce Context Unrolling: an explicit intermediate reasoning stage where modal representations are iteratively exchanged, aligned and aggregated before final decoding.
Leverage the aggregated multimodal representation to produce predictions that better reflect complementary information across modalities.
impact: Enables more accurate and faithful multimodal reasoning and fusion, improving downstream performance and interpretability for practitioners building vision+language, video, and 3D-aware applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing modalities feeding into the Omni model, then an explicit 'Context Unrolling' block (iterative steps) before final output.
Icon grid of modalities (text, image, video, 3D, latent) converging into a single aggregated representation.
Before/after comparison chart (performance or fidelity) illustrating gains from Context Unrolling vs. naive fusion.
Schematic of iterative attention/exchange during unrolling to highlight the intermediate reasoning process.
paper_authors: Ceyuan Yang, Zhijie Lin, Yang Zhao, Fei Xiao, Hao He
